headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API/webhook surfaces can amplify prompt injection and data leakage when paired with a non-runnable, read-only catalog agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable collection with no shared channel shown, but Agent B exposes MCP/server-style tool surfaces and can ingest external content. If A’s outputs are copied into B or surfaced through shared workspace/MCP, B could treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF A’s content is pasted or synced into B’s MCP/API inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF B parses catalog text as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A-generated text into B.
Add provenance tags to all A-originated content before B reads it.
Require a human review step before B executes any instruction-like text.
Restrict B MCP tools to allowlisted actions only.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A shows no data classes touched and no egress, while B touches governance and memory-related metadata and can call APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. If they share a workspace or B receives A’s files, B could transmit that content outward. Because the shared-storage path is not documented, this is an inferred medium risk rather than high.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem or message bus, B can read A-originated artifacts.
IF B forwards received content through APIs/webhooks, any shared sensitive material can leak externally.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Block B from receiving raw files unless necessary.
Turn off webhook/API forwarding for shared artifacts.
Review B’s outbound destinations before enabling integrations.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capability shown, and B’s profile only states multiple instances plus API/MCP-style surfaces. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable writes to the same resource, so direct conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because B’s write scopes are unspecified, but the documented overlap is too weak for medium.
conditions: IF B is configured with write access to the same external resource as A’s outputs, conflicts can occur.
IF both agents mutate the same shared state without locking, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces to A and B.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared destinations.
Add a lock or queue around any shared mutable resource.
Check B’s write scopes before enabling integrations.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic-concurrency or locking for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated collection and not an action-taking agent, while B is a data-engineering system that can consume APIs, events, webhooks, and MCP inputs. If A’s outputs are used as authoritative references inside B, B may propagate stale or incorrect catalog facts downstream. The pathway exists by inference, but no direct verification loop is documented.
conditions: IF B treats A’s text as authoritative without validation, errors can cascade into downstream metadata or workflows.
IF A’s content is used as a source of facts for B, B may render or act on incorrect information.
mitigations: Require source verification before B accepts A-derived facts.
Mark A content as untrusted reference material.
Add a review step for any B action based on A output.
Limit B to read-only use of A unless validated.
requires-engineering: add provenance and validation gates in B’s ingestion pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source, non-runnable collection with no data classes touched, so it presents no clear residency or retention issue. B touches governance and memory metadata and may process operational metadata, but the profile does not show a specific regulated data class or jurisdiction mismatch. The compliance pathway is therefore weak and mostly contingent on external deployment choices.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is loaded into B, its API/webhook/MCP handling must match the deployment’s residency and retention rules.
IF A is used only as a static open-source reference, no compliance breach is indicated.
mitigations: Confirm what data classes B will store before enabling it.
Disable retention for any regulated metadata if not required.
Keep A as a static reference only.
Review B’s webhook/API destinations for jurisdiction.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to B’s deployment.
